title.narrative: Nanjing Qinhuai River Environmental Improvement Project

description.narrative: The Project will help Nanjing, the capital city of Jiangsu Province, in (i) reducing water pollution; (ii) protecting water resources; (iii) reducing economic losses and disruption to livelihoods from frequent localized flooding; (iv) promoting sustainable economic development; (v) improving the environment, living conditions, and public health standards; (vi) developing an integrated wastewater and sludge management system; and (vii) improving service efficiency through increased competition and private sector participation. The Project includes 10 major activities grouped into six components: (i) Inner Qinhuai River sewerage and water replenishment, (ii) City East wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) and sewerage system, (iii) North HeXi District sewerage, river improvement, and water replenishment, (iv) stormwater drainage, (v) sludge treatment and disposal component, and (vi) institutional development. All components of the Project contribute to significantly improving water quality of the Qinhuai River, which empties into the Yangtze River. The Project supports the Government's 11th Five-Year Plan, which includes goals of improving living conditions and health in cities and promoting their sustainable economic development.

description.narrative: Improved management of surface water resources in Nanjing city (contributing to the achievement of Millennium Development Goal 7, target 10)

By 2013, water quality of the Qinhuai River improved from worse than class V in 2006 to class IV Progress/Status: In 2011, water quality of the Upper Qinhuai River improved significantly and met the target of Class IV; while the water quality of the Inner Qinhuai River systems and other rivers in Hexi District is still worse than Class IV, but the concentrations of most parameters have notably decreased. By 2011, water quality of the Qinhuai River has improved from worse than class V in 2006 to class IV in 2011 Data Source: Wastewater effluent quality and monitoring data Actual value:

Frequency of disruption and damage due to local stormwater flooding reduced by more than 50% by 2013 Progress/Status: At completion of component (2009), frequency of disruption and damage due to local stormwater flooding has decreased from the baseline 0.74 incidence per annum to 0.44 incidence per annum in August 2009 survey, moving towards the target of 0.37 Data Source: Nanjing statistical yearbook Actual value:

Wastewater treatment rate increased from the current level of 75% to 85% by 2013 Progress/Status: Municipal wastewater treatment rate increased to 85% by Aug 2009 and further increased to 95% by 2011 Data Source: Municipal sludge disposal records Actual value:

By 2013, annual wastewater effluent pollutant loading is reduced by 5,000 tons biochemical oxygen demand, 9,000 tons chemical oxygen demand, 6,800 tons suspended solids, 950 tons ammonia nitrogen, and 110 tons total phosphorous Progress/Status: At full capacity of WWTP (2014), annual wastewater effluent pollutant loading is reduced by around 4,380 tons BOD, 10,267 tons COD, 8,572 tons suspended solids, 2,008 tons ammonia nitrogen, and 148 tons total phosphorous. Data Source: Water supply data (rate of utilization and flow volumes) Base year: 2006 Baseline value: N

Municipal sludge treatment and disposal significantly improved by 2013 Progress/Status: Despite cancellation of component E, the output was completed through domestic funds, as NMG has contracted out the required sludge treatment of 570 m3 per day for a period of 10 years Data Source: ADB review missions
Government's project completion report Base year: 2006 Baseline value: N

Probability of flooding incidence in the Qinhuai River and its tributaries is reduced from an average of once every 40 years, and the ecological environment of the Qinhuai River and its tributaries is improved through soil conservation, and rive water replenishment by 2013 Progress/Status: Probability of flooding incidence for the Qinhuai River mainstream is once in 50 years, and that for the tributaries is about 20 years. The ecological environment of the Qinhuai River and its tributaries has improved through dredging and ecological restoration of revetment by 2011. Data Source: River flood-gauging station data and flood map and records Base year: 2006 Baseline value: N
